strategies.title: [bounded-ejection-chain] Two-transaction local-minimum escape
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: bounded-ejection-chain  
Replacement scope: Replace the current `improve` phase’s single adjacent-swap and single-transaction relocation neighborhood after each constructed schedule.  
Compute budget: At most 16 ejection-chain trials per locally optimized incumbent; each trial removes two distinct transactions and evaluates at most 48 reinsertion arrangements, followed by at most 20 accepted ordinary relocation improvements. This adds at most 768 true-cost evaluations per incumbent and should remain within a 105-second per-workload budget.  
Gain mechanism: The observed incumbent already uses single relocation descent and reached total makespan 262, so its main bottleneck is likely local minima in the one-transaction insertion neighborhood. An ejection chain removes two transactions simultaneously, then reinserts the first transaction into each candidate position and the second into each candidate position of the resulting sequence, considering both removal orders. This can cross a barrier where neither transaction can improve alone but their coordinated order can reduce a conflict chain. Keep only strict true-cost improvements, maintain a cached `get_opt_seq_cost`, and preserve a complete permutation by removing exactly two unique IDs and reinserting both before evaluation. Start from the current valid incumbent so timeout always returns that complete permutation. Expected-gain check: this exposes paired reorderings that the incumbent’s strict one-transaction local search cannot realize in one move; it is falsified if the evaluator’s total recomputed makespan remains at least 262, while any total at most 261 yields \(1000000/(1+261)=3816.79\), strictly above 3802.28.

strategies.title: [ruin-recreate-lns] Mesoscopic destroy-and-exact-repair search
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ruin-recreate-lns  
Replacement scope: Replace the repeated independent randomized-greedy restarts after the first locally optimized schedule with an incumbent-centered ruin-and-recreate phase.  
Compute budget: At most 14 ruin/recreate attempts per workload. On attempt \(q\), remove a random subset of `max(3, n // 10)` transaction IDs from the incumbent, shuffle that removed set, and reinsert each removed transaction at its exact best position by evaluating every insertion position in the current partial order. Apply at most 24 accepted adjacent/relocation descent moves afterward. Stop at the 105-second workload deadline.  
Gain mechanism: A random greedy restart changes the whole prefix history and spends many calls rediscovering obvious choices; it does not deliberately preserve the good parts of the 262-cost schedule while changing the conflict-heavy region. Ruin/recreate holds approximately 90% of an already good transaction topology fixed and jointly changes the ordering and attachment positions of a mesoscopic subsystem. Exact best-position repair uses the simulator objective rather than transaction length or write count. Accept repaired schedules only when their final true cost is better, and always retain the original full permutation as fallback. Removal and reinsertion are bijective, so every returned schedule remains a complete permutation of `range(workload.num_txns)`. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is joint reattachment of a removed transaction subsystem around fixed transactions, which neither a fresh prefix-greedy construction nor one-item descent can enforce; the hypothesis is falsified if no evaluator run obtains total makespan below 262.

strategies.title: [sampled-best-insertion] Structural NEH-style transaction construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: sampled-best-insertion  
Replacement scope: Replace `greedy_order`, which irrevocably appends one transaction to the end of a prefix, with a sampled best-insertion constructor.  
Compute budget: Build at most four schedules per workload. Begin each with a different random transaction; at every construction depth sample at most seven remaining transactions, evaluate every insertion position for each sampled transaction, and insert the transaction-position pair with lowest exact prefix cost. Finish immediately by appending unplaced IDs if the 105-second deadline is reached; otherwise locally improve the finished schedule for at most 35 accepted moves.  
Gain mechanism: The current constructor has an append-only topology: once a transaction is selected early, it can only move later through expensive local refinement, and its random tie selection is usually ineffective because the pool contains only exactly tied costs. Best insertion directly permits a later-discovered transaction to be placed before, between, or after all prior transactions during construction. Sampling several candidate transactions controls the cubic cost while retaining genuine construction diversity. All trial prefixes contain unique IDs; completion appends each remaining ID once; and final candidates are checked by the true simulator cost before becoming incumbent. Expected-gain check: this construction can create an early/interior transaction placement that append-only greedy cannot create at the same prefix depth, and the hypothesis is falsified unless the recomputed total makespan falls below the incumbent 262 threshold.

strategies.title: [exact-window-permutation] Contiguous critical-window exact reordering
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: exact-window-permutation  
Replacement scope: Replace the current bounded two-transaction ejection-chain loop inside `improve`, retaining the constructor and final single-transaction relocation descent.  
Compute budget: At most 16 distinct contiguous windows per constructed schedule; enumerate all `5! = 120` permutations of each window, with a strict wall-clock deadline and no additional construction starts. This is approximately 1,920 exact-cost evaluations per start, comparable to the incumbent pair-move evaluation volume.  
Gain mechanism: The observed bottleneck is that makespan remains 235 despite pair moves, indicating local barriers involving more than two mutually conflicting transactions. For each selected five-transaction contiguous region, hold every outside transaction fixed and exactly optimize the internal transaction ordering. This introduces a joint five-way precedence/contact topology that neither a single relocation nor the incumbent’s sampled pair positions can guarantee it evaluates. Each accepted window is a complete permutation replacement, so schedule validity is preserved automatically; initialization and all failed trials retain a valid incumbent schedule. The falsifiable improvement hypothesis is that resolving one critical five-transaction conflict chain can reduce the three-workload total makespan from 235 to at most 234, which would raise `combined_score` to `1000000 / 235 = 4255.319...`, strictly above 4237.288.

strategies.title: [prefix-beam-construction] Cost-ranked beam construction over partial schedules
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: prefix-beam-construction  
Replacement scope: Replace `best_insertion_order` and the loop selecting its starting transactions with a width-4 beam of distinct partial schedules; retain a bounded local improvement phase afterward.  
Compute budget: Use 3 independent beam seeds, beam width 4, expand at most 8 unplaced transactions from each beam member at every depth, and test every insertion position for each expanded transaction. Stop expansion at the shared 105-second per-workload deadline, immediately completing any surviving prefix by appending its unplaced IDs.  
Gain mechanism: The observed constructor greedily commits to a single cheapest insertion at every stage, so an early partial-order tie or near-tie cannot be reconsidered even when it creates an expensive late conflict chain. A beam preserves four competing prefix topologies and lets later exact partial-sequence costs eliminate bad early choices. Deduplicate beam states by tuple, retain the lowest exact cost states, and append missing IDs only if time expires, thereby always returning a full transaction-ID permutation. The falsifiable improvement hypothesis is that a beam survivor with a different early ordering can attain total makespan at most 234 after the existing improvement phase; the evaluator threshold is therefore raw total makespan `<= 234` rather than an ungrounded score prediction.

strategies.title: [adjacent-block-relocation] Exhaustive two-operation block relocation descent
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: adjacent-block-relocation  
Replacement scope: Replace the final randomized single-item relocation loop in `improve` with a variable-neighborhood descent that first exhaustively relocates an adjacent two-transaction block, in both internal orders, then applies one exhaustive single-transaction relocation pass.  
Compute budget: At most 10 accepted block moves and 8 accepted single relocations per start. For each block move, inspect every source block and every legal destination boundary, testing the preserved and reversed block order; terminate immediately on deadline. This has no extra optimizer starts and is bounded by roughly `20 * n * n` exact evaluations in the worst accepted-move case.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can move two selected transactions but samples only a small set of source pairs and reinsertion pairs; it does not systematically preserve or reverse an adjacent conflict-producing chain while moving it across every possible boundary. Adjacent block relocation changes the schedule’s contact topology by moving a coupled producer/consumer pair together, avoiding the transient separation that can make each constituent single relocation non-improving. Removing a two-element slice and reinserting its IDs preserves a complete permutation in every trial, with the pre-improvement schedule retained as fallback. The falsifiable improvement hypothesis is that at least one currently missed adjacent conflict pair can be moved across its blocking interval and reduce total makespan to `<= 234`; otherwise the evaluator will reject it against the current raw makespan 235 baseline.

strategies.title: [reverse-conditioned-insertion] Bidirectional suffix/prefix NEH construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: reverse-conditioned-insertion  
Replacement scope: Replace the current forward-only `construct(start)` phase with a split portfolio of forward prefix insertion and backward suffix insertion, while retaining the existing exact-window and relocation improvement phase.  
Compute budget: Four total construction starts per workload: three forward and one backward; retain the existing eight sampled transaction candidates per insertion and the existing 105-second per-workload deadline. Evaluation-time effect is approximately neutral because the number of starts and insertion evaluations is unchanged.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can only decide where a transaction belongs relative to an already-built prefix. A backward construction instead builds a suffix and evaluates reversed partial schedules, allowing late conflict-causing writers to be placed first in the construction representation and thereby creating final schedules with different global conflict-release topology. Both constructions return complete permutations by appending every remaining transaction before finalizing orientation, and the best true full-schedule cost remains the returned result. The observed bottleneck is that all incumbent starts share the same forward insertion bias, so exact local improvement begins from closely related precedence topologies; this replacement supplies a geometrically opposite seed without weakening the proven local search. Expected-gain check: improvement is falsified unless the three-workload true makespan total is at most 232, which would yield \(1{,}000{,}000/(1+232)=4291.845\), strictly above 4273.504; the incumbent cannot create suffix-conditioned insertion decisions during construction.

strategies.title: [supertransaction-block-order] Exact coarsened block-order optimization
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: supertransaction-block-order  
Replacement scope: Replace the final single-transaction relocation loop in `improve` with a mesoscopic phase that partitions the current schedule into consecutive blocks and exactly optimizes the ordering of those blocks while preserving each block’s internal order.  
Compute budget: At most two block partitions per improved schedule: one into at most five equal consecutive blocks and one shifted partition with the same maximum; enumerate at most \(5! = 120\) block orders for each partition, stopping at the existing deadline. Evaluation-time effect is bounded by 240 full schedule evaluations per construction start, substantially below the existing five-window permutation budget.  
Gain mechanism: A block is treated as a supertransaction, so one move changes many cross-block read/write precedence contacts simultaneously while retaining proven local order inside each block. This is not pair or adjacent-block relocation: the optimizer can jointly choose the order of all blocks, including non-adjacent blocks, which is a mesoscopic subsystem replacement unavailable to the incumbent’s first-improving one-transaction move. Build blocks by splitting the schedule into nearly equal nonempty consecutive chunks, concatenate blocks in each tested permutation, and accept only the lowest actual simulator cost; every trial is automatically a complete permutation. The observed bottleneck is that the current final phase can require several individually non-improving relocations to realize a beneficial global reversal of transaction groups. Expected-gain check: improvement is falsified unless the resulting true aggregate makespan is at most 232; the new degree of freedom is a joint permutation of up to five transaction groups, which the incumbent relocation descent cannot evaluate as one atomic transformation.

strategies.title: [dispersed-position-kopt] Noncontiguous exact positional reordering
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: dispersed-position-kopt  
Replacement scope: Replace half of the contiguous five-transaction window enumeration in `improve` with exact five-transaction permutations over dispersed schedule positions, retaining the remaining contiguous adaptive windows and the incumbent constructor.  
Compute budget: Optimize at most eight contiguous windows and at most eight dispersed five-position sets per start; each set has at most \(5!-1=119\) evaluated alternatives. Construct dispersed sets deterministically from five approximately equally spaced positions, plus shifted versions, and stop at the current deadline. Evaluation-time effect is no greater than the incumbent’s sixteen five-window searches.  
Gain mechanism: Contiguous windows only modify transactions already adjacent in the current schedule. A dispersed set selects one transaction from each schedule region, then jointly changes their relative order while leaving all unselected transactions fixed; this directly exposes long-range writer/reader contacts that cannot enter one contiguous window. Use positions derived from evenly spaced indices and cyclic shifts, discard duplicate position sets, extract transactions at those positions, test all permutations by writing them back to exactly those positions, and retain the lowest true cost. This preserves validity because it merely permutes five existing unique IDs. The observed bottleneck is that adaptive contiguous inspection emphasizes overlap around accepted local changes but has no move that can jointly reorder distant conflict participants. Expected-gain check: improvement is falsified unless the total true makespan reaches at most 232; the falsifiable new transformation is an exact permutation of separated positions, which no contiguous five-position permutation in the incumbent can represent.

strategies.title: [regret-guided-insertion] Conflict-sensitive regret construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: regret-guided-insertion  
Replacement scope: Replace `construct(start)` with a sampled regret-insertion constructor; retain the exact-cost cache and the incumbent’s bounded improvement phase.  
Compute budget: At each construction step, evaluate at most 8 sampled remaining transactions across all insertion positions; use at most 4 starts. This has approximately the same cost-call scale as the current sampled insertion constructor and no material evaluation-time increase.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent chooses the transaction with the lowest immediate insertion cost, which can postpone a transaction whose feasible low-cost positions are rare. For every sampled candidate, compute its best and second-best insertion cost, then choose the transaction with the greatest regret (`second_best - best_best`), breaking ties by lower best cost. This explicitly prioritizes transactions that would become expensive if delayed, a degree of freedom absent from immediate-best insertion. The schedule remains valid because each transaction is removed from `remaining` exactly once and inserted once; any deadline path appends every unplaced ID in deterministic order.  
Observed bottleneck: sampled insertion has a myopic candidate-selection rule even though it evaluates multiple insertion positions. Concrete change: choose among sampled candidates using exact insertion regret rather than only the single lowest partial-schedule cost. Falsifiable improvement hypothesis: this construction is useful only if the evaluator finds total true makespan at most 232, which yields `1000000 / 233 = 4291.845...`, strictly above 4273.504274.

strategies.title: [pairwise-preference-topology] Pair-conflict tournament seed
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: pairwise-preference-topology  
Replacement scope: Replace the random-start portion of the construction phase with a deterministic pairwise-preference seed followed by exact sequential insertion; keep one incumbent-style randomized construction as fallback diversification.  
Compute budget: Evaluate both two-transaction orders for every unordered pair, at most `n*(n-1)` exact cost calls; create one tournament-based seed and apply no more than 12 exact local windows plus 10 accepted relocations. For 100 transactions this is at most 9,900 pair evaluations, materially smaller than a full all-transaction insertion search.  
Gain mechanism: For each pair `(i, j)`, compare exact costs of `[i, j]` and `[j, i]`. Treat the difference as a directed preference margin, rank transactions by net outgoing preference margin, and insert transactions in that global conflict-informed order using exact insertion positions. This changes construction topology from independently randomized starts to a schedule-wide ordering derived from measured conflict direction. It captures whether placing one transaction before another consistently reduces serialization delay, including read-write versus write-write asymmetry. Validity is preserved because the final sequential insertion is a permutation construction and unfinished transactions are appended.  
Observed bottleneck: the current constructor sees partial schedules but has no global estimate of which transaction pairs should consistently be ordered first. Concrete change: use exact two-transaction scheduling evaluations to build a weighted precedence tournament before constructing the full permutation. Falsifiable improvement hypothesis: the pairwise seed adds a globally coordinated precedence direction that the incumbent’s random starts cannot represent, and it succeeds only if its returned schedule reduces the measured total makespan below 233.

strategies.title: [triple-ejection-descent] Three-transaction coordinated escape
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: triple-ejection-descent  
Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent’s final single-transaction relocation loop with bounded three-transaction ejection-chain descent after the exact-window phase.  
Compute budget: At most 10 chain attempts per constructed schedule; each attempt selects three separated positions, removes their transactions, tests all 6 reinsertion orders and bounded reinsertion position combinations centered around their original gaps, accepting only strict exact-cost improvements. Follow with at most 8 ordinary strict relocations. This is bounded below the cost of exhaustive unrestricted three-item relocation.  
Gain mechanism: A single relocation cannot cross barriers where three transactions mutually block one another through separate conflicting keys. Removing three transactions simultaneously permits changing their relative order and moving each across a different conflict boundary in one accepted move. This is a new coordinated escape direction beyond the incumbent’s contiguous permutation windows and one-item relocation descent. Every trial starts from a permutation, removes three distinct IDs, and reinserts exactly those same IDs, preserving validity.  
Observed bottleneck: exact contiguous windows cannot move transactions across distant separators, while individual relocation can be trapped when no one transaction improves alone. Concrete change: use bounded noncontiguous three-item ejection chains with all six internal orders and strict true-cost acceptance. Falsifiable improvement hypothesis: this succeeds if a schedule that is locally stable under the incumbent’s one-item relocation can be improved by one accepted coordinated three-item move and the evaluator reports total makespan at most 232.
